solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Burning's burning sensation

parts.note: burning means hot, and the apostrophe-s adds an S
burning means hot

explanation.surface: A fever's hot, stinging feeling described twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning sensation' reads as one phrase, but only 'sensation' is the definition; the two burnings give HOT + S + HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a person causing a stir, a star performer, which is what a hotshot is.

clue.text: Bob, perhaps, one inspired by tough love

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the word for tough takes in the numeral

parts.note: tough means hard
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Bob, maybe a person, is someone moved by tough love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, so it is an example of a styled head of hair.

clue.text: Address nail left on top of escritoire

parts.note: a tack is a small nail

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter, as this is a down clue

explanation.surface: Fixing an address label with a nail, left on top of a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: An escritoire is a writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it, to grapple with it.

clue.text: Treasure something sweet on some bananas, say?

parts.note: honey is a sweet food made by bees
bananas grow and are sold in bunches; say flags the example

explanation.surface: A sweet treat drizzled on bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasure' is a term of endearment here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate names for a loved one, sweetheart-style endearments.

clue.text: Physicist entering coordinates latterly

indicators.note: entering means the answer goes into the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A scientist logging coordinates late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the answer is concealed in coordinaTES LAtterly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American scientist and inventor behind alternating current systems.

clue.text: Part right, but on the periphery

indicators.note: the word for but sits around the outside of the letter for right

parts.note: but, in the sense of save or other than, means except

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a point is partly right, though only marginally.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a part taken from a longer text, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Looking up, disease on the way in alien world far away

indicators.note: in puts the reversed disease and road inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the reversed disease above the road word
looking up reads the word upwards in this down clue

parts.note: pox is a disease
a lane is a way, a road

explanation.surface: Looking skyward at a distant planet with a disease on the road there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' reverses the disease, as this is a down clue, and ET is the film's alien, which takes the rest in.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet orbiting a star other than the Sun is a distant world beyond our solar system.

clue.text: Some talking bird

definitions.meaning: a bit of conversation, a natter
a stonechat or whinchat, a small songbird

explanation.definitionFit: Informal conversation is idle talk, and a group of small songbirds share the same name.

clue.text: Controller of current that rose at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sea current that rose, and whatever controls it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests the sea; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor regulates the flow of electricity in a circuit.

clue.text: Bully, time and time again taken down

parts.note: a second time unit, hour, abbreviated HR
something eaten has been swallowed, taken down

explanation.surface: A bully keeps getting knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, the verb in each case.

clue.text: South American once preserved?

definitions.meaning: a member of the old Peruvian empire, now gone
food put up in a tin is, read as two words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an ancient South American has been kept intact, like a mummy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into IN CAN: tinned food is preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the empire of the Andes that the Spanish conquered in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Advertising professional in general so phoney

indicators.note: phoney means fake, so these letters are a false arrangement to be reworked

explanation.surface: An ad man is, broadly speaking, a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phoney' rearranges GENERALSO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of catchy slogans for campaigns is a coiner of advertising lines.

clue.text: Herb accompanying woman back, extremely lazy to vacillate

parts.note: dill is a feathery culinary herb

indicators.note: back says the word for woman is read from its end

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: extremely picks out the two ends of the word lazy

explanation.surface: A recipe-like scene: a herb, a woman returning, and someone too idle to make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LADY into YDAL; the ends of lazy give LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither or dawdle is to waver and waste time without deciding, the infinitive matching the infinitive.

clue.text: Article on Thailand, mostly — and where it is?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: mostly means the old name for Thailand loses its final letter

parts.note: Siam is the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A piece written about Thailand, largely, followed by a question about its location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to Thailand: SIA from SIAM less its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand lies in the continent stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Dry soldier disturbed drunk partner?

indicators.note: disturbed means upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sober soldier is upset by his inebriated companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges DRYSOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The police charge is 'drunk and disorderly', so the word partners drunk in that phrase.

clue.text: Verify gold teeth? I can't when false

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: false teeth are not the real thing, so the letters here are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dentist asked to confirm gold teeth are genuine admits they can't if the set is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when false' scrambles the letters of teeth, I and can't; gold is its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something as genuine, such as a signature or an antique, is to verify it.

clue.text: In on

definitions.meaning: on means taking place, under way

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fashionable and lively, and taking place now, as an event occurring.

clue.text: Female with organ removed, afraid of nothing

parts.note: without ears, the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A woman who has lost an organ is unafraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being brave and bold means having no fright at all.

clue.text: Ball slower? Second hurries up

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

indicators.note: up reads the word for hurries upwards in this down clue

parts.note: nips means hurries, as in nipping out

explanation.surface: A slow ball bowled, with someone hurrying for a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a unit of time; it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse rotation on a ball makes it check and slow after bouncing, as in tennis or snooker.

clue.text: In manifestation of God, image recalled freedom

indicators.note: in places the reversed picture word inside the theological term

parts.note: an emanation is something flowing out from God as a manifestation of the divine

indicators.note: recalled means the word for image is called back, read backwards

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A religious claim that a recalled divine vision brought liberation.
explanation.walkthrough: In theology an emanation is something flowing forth from God; 'recalled' reverses the image word before 'In' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Emancipation is release from slavery or restriction, so it amounts to liberty.

clue.text: Island taking a wallop in the midst of action

indicators.note: taking means the middle letters take in the other pieces
the midst of picks the central pair of letters

parts.note: to wallop is to hit

explanation.surface: An island where someone takes a punch in the middle of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of action is TI, which takes A + HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest of French Polynesia's Society group in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Flower bearing towards the back

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A flower carrying itself to the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, rearwards means towards the stern.

clue.text: Collector — of girlfriends?

parts.note: the garden tool gathers up leaves, and a womanising roué gathers lovers

explanation.surface: Someone who collects things, the question being whether the collection is of girlfriends.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden tool collects leaves; the same word is an old term for a dissolute womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine or playboy, in old-fashioned usage, is a man who pursues many women.

clue.text: Where pub landlords are in prison

definitions.meaning: a pub landlord works on the far side of the counter

explanation.walkthrough: A pub's bar is its serving counter, so landlords stand on the far side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being locked up puts a convict on the far side of the cell's metal grille, an idiom for imprisonment.

clue.text: Fire in valley extinguished at the bottom

indicators.note: the bottom letter of the valley word is put out, in this down clue

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A fire in a valley is put out at its base.
explanation.definitionFit: An inglenook is beside a hearth, and the word itself is an old term for a domestic blaze.

clue.text: Ultimate in diseases one's caught, evidence of chickenpox, say?

indicators.note: ultimate picks out the final letter of diseases

parts.note: a taxi is something one catches

explanation.surface: A doctor notes the last of the diseases picked up, chickenpox showing as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' suggests infection; it is catching a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust forming over a healing chickenpox spot is a sign of the illness.

clue.text: Old setter good with child

parts.note: ex means former, old
pectin is what makes jam set

explanation.surface: An ageing setter, good with children, as a dog might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests a dog or the crossword compiler; here it is the gelling agent in jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are euphemisms for being pregnant, carrying a baby.

clue.text: Lift some valuables I, arguably, must return

indicators.note: return means the extracted letters are read backwards
some means only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone argues they ought to give back some of the valuables they lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ESIAR from valuables I, arguably; 'must return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it, push it higher.

clue.text: Possible ballast to drop, with balloon initially secured?

indicators.note: secured means the middle letters are held fast inside the word for drop

parts.note: to sag is to droop, drop
and means with, in addition to

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of balloon

explanation.surface: A balloonist's ballast, ready to be dropped once the balloon is tethered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with balloon initially' supplies the middle letters, which 'secured' holds inside the word for drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-air balloons carry sacks of sand as weight to be released for height, so one is an example of ballast.

clue.text: Like paradise, any isle in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Any island seems heavenly when a storm is raging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges ANYISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysian Fields were the Greek afterlife's blessed realm, so the adjective means heavenly.
